Prayer in the present petition filed under Section 482 of the BNSS, 2023 is for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner in case FIR No.06 dated 15.01.2026 registered under Sections 420 and 120-B of IPC, at Police Station Ghall Khurd, District Ferozepur.
2. On 25.02.2026, following order had been passed: -

"Prayer in the present petition filed under Section 482 of the BNSS, 2023 is for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner in case FIR No.06 dated 15.01.2026 registered under Sections 420 and 120-B of IPC, at Police Station Ghall Khurd, District Ferozepur.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He argued that as per the prosecution case, the daughter of the petitioner (Babbaldeep Kaur) got married with son of the complainant (Kamaljeet Singh) on 06.02.2018.

He further argued that initially, study visa for Australia was applied by the CRM-M-10927-2026 daughter of the petitioner,
which was refused by the Australia Embassy as per its norms but the complainant levelled false allegations against the petitioner and her daughter that because of this refusal, he has suffered loss of Rs.12 lakhs.

It is further submitted that later study visa for Canada was applied by the daughter of the petitioner with the consent of the complainant and her husband, which was approved and she went to Canada in April,
2021.

He argued that from the date of marriage i.e. 06.02.2018 till April 2021,

1 the petitioner never interfered into the matrimonial life of his daughter.

sentences.text:
Thereafier,
daughter of the petitioner submitted necessary documents for grant of spouse visa for Canada and the same was granted in the year 2022 and her husbnad arrived at Canada.

He argued that thereatter false allegations have been levelled by the complainant that the daughter of the petitioner had not received Kamaljeet Singh (son of the complainant) at Airport but in fact, Kamaljeet Singh did not inform her about his arrival at Canada and he started residing there with another woman as he did not want to reside with Babbaldeep Kaur.

He argued that spouse visa of the son of the complainant is going to expire in March, 2026 and the allegation of demanding Rs.40 lakhs more from the complainant, in order to renew the same, is totally false and frivolous, only to put pressure upon the petitioner and his daughter for compromising the matrimonial dispute.
He argued that no offence under Sections 420 and 120- B are made out against the petitioner as the contents of the FIR, even on face of it did not fulfill the ingredients of the said sections.
Moreover, the petitioner has clean antecedents as he is not involved in any other case and no recovery is to be eftected from him.
Learned counsel has further submitted that the petitioner is ready and willing to join the investigation as and when called upon to do so by the investigating agency.
Notice of motion.

On asking of the Court, Mr. Ravinder Singh, DAG, Punjab,
accepts notice on behalf of respondent-State and seeks time to file status report in the matter.
Adjourned to 06.03.2026.

In the meantime, the petitioner is directed to join investigation within a week from today and would appear as and when required by the Investigating Officer and cooperate with the Investigating Agency.
In the event of arrest, he shall be admitted to interim bail on furnishing of bail/surety bonds to the satisfaction of Arresting/Investigating Officer.
The petitioner shall also abide by the conditions as envisaged under Section 482(2) of BNSS, 2023."
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in compliance of the order dated 25.02.2026 passed by this Court, the petitioner has joined the investigation.
4. Learned counsel for the State, on instructions from ASI Harjinder Singh, has submitted that the petitioner has joined the investigation and is no longer required for further investigation.
5. In view of the statement made by learned State counsel, the interim order dated 25.02.2026 is made absolute.
The petitioner shall continue to join investigation, as and when called by the Investigating Officer and shall also abide by the conditions as provided under Section 482(2) of the BNSS.
